title: Welcome to the CBCS Coding Club!
text:
Welcome to the CBCS Coding Club!



Our vision
CBCS Coding Club is a student-led group that aims to provide a common space for coding and programming geeks and enthusiasts alike to interact and share their passion about coding. The CBCS Coding Club comprises Higher Degree by Research (HDR) students and Early Career Researchers (ECRs) in the Centre for Biodiversity and Conservation Science (CBCS) as well as the School of the Environment (SENV) at the University of Queensland. The club’s vision is to provide a space for the gathering of like-minded coders and programmers in the fields of conservation and environmental science regardless of their levels of coding expertise.


Join us!
💻 Do you love coding?
💡 Are you interested in learning more about coding?
🤔 Do you want to improve your coding skills but don’t know where to start?
🔥 Do you feel the burning urge to geek out about your favorite package or function?
If your answer is yes to any of those questions, then Join Coding Club!

title: Join us
text:
We are an inclusive bunch, so to be part of the growing CBCS Coding Club community, all you need to do is ask and email the Current Co-leads to be added.
For any questions regarding the Centre for Biodiversity and Conservation Science, please email cbcs-info@uq.edu.au.

title: Coding Resources
text: Part of the CBCS Coding Club’s initiative is to compile a list of different coding resources that could support environmental and conservation research. This compilation is ‘alive’, and so if there are any resources that you think are missing from the list below (we know that we are missing lots!), please do contact any of the current coding club leads and we can add them.

title: Coding Resources
text:
Data wrangling and analysis

janitor for cleaning up messy data
here for setting working directories
purrr for functional programming in loops made easy!
furrr combining purrr with future’s parallel capabilities

title: Coding Resources
text:
Spatial wrangling and analysis

terra for wrangling and analyzing raster (and vector!) data
sf for wrangling and analyzing vector data

title: Coding Resources
text:
Visualization

ggplot2 for all-around visualizations, and great for visualizing sf objects using primarily geom_sf()
tmap for thematic mapping
leaflet for creating interactive maps
tidyterra for visualizing terra objects using ggplot2
patchwork for stitching together different plots

title: Who are we?
text: The CBCS Coding Club comprises a group of students and early career researchers in CBCS and SENV at the University of Queensland. Coding Club is currently co-led by:

title: Who are we?
text:
Liana van Woesik



 

Liana is a PhD student working on the Moreton Bay region of Queensland, Australia where she focuses on data analysis of water-quality, land–sea conservation planning and management, marine science, and pollution impacts on coastal ecosystems. Liana loves coding in R for its powerful statistics, amazing data-visualization tools, and huge ecosystem of packages that facilitate impactful science.

title: Who are we?
text:
Ben Lucas



  

Ben is an ecological connectivity researcher, looking into enhancing connectivity implementation under the global biodiversity framework via clarifying conceptual gaps and comparing methods of connectivity measurement. Ben works with R, Julia, NetLogo, and Bash, but also has interest in Python and statistical inference approaches.

title: Who are we?
text:
Angela Liu



 

Angela is a PhD student studying the migratory connectivity of marine megavertebrates, and how policy and spatial planning can better integrate these species. Angela primarily works in R, and she is interested in movement modelling, network analysis, and spatial prioritization.

title: Rule 1
text:
Joining Coding Club is easy, but our members also follow some simple (and straightforward) rules:

Rule 1
Be nice. Be respectful. Be inclusive. 👥


Rule 2
We’ll all learn from each other. It’s a give and take. 🤝


Rule 3
We are not required to host workshops. There are better resources for these, and we would gladly point you to these resources if needed. 📔
Coding club is just as good as its members. So if you like what Coding Club is doing, support the club by participating in meet-ups and events and being more active.

title: Past Meet-ups
text:
CBCS Coding Club meet-ups are led by different folks of different coding backgrounds and career levels. Topics are broad and encompass different programming languages (R, python), coding skills (spatial data analysis and visualization, data wrangling, writing shiny apps), and coding tools (VS Code, HPC).
If you’re interested in leading a meet-up, feel free to contact any of the current Coding Club co-leads!
